news.title: Gas Prices Are High Now, but for Many Americans They Were Even Higher in the Past
news.summary_en: Gas prices have surged amid the Iran conflict, but adjusted for inflation and wages, 2008 was costlier.

news.title: On Facebook and Instagram, Political Ads Are Increasingly Critical of Data Centers
news.summary_en: Political ads about data centers on Facebook and Instagram have turned increasingly critical, with 57% opposed and just 3% supportive ahead of the midterms.

news.title: The 2026 Midterms Will Be Uniquely Difficult for Polls
news.summary_en: Polls haven’t gotten worse, but fake respondents, synthetic AI surveys and election unknowns make the 2026 midterms uniquely hard to poll.

news.title: Americans Are Open to AI in Healthcare, but Want Humans Making Final Calls
news.summary_en: Americans are generally open to AI handling administrative and medical tasks, but they largely don’t want AI operating without human oversight. About half (47%) say AI will make the relationship between patients and their doctors worse, compared with 10% who say it will make it better.

news.title: 17 States Haven’t Had a Woman Governor, and 15 Haven’t Had a Woman Senator
news.summary_en: Today, women currently hold a record 27 of the Senate’s 100 seats, and women hold the office of governor in 14 of the 50 states.

news.title: Most Americans’ Religious Lives Haven’t Changed Much in Recent Years
news.summary_en: Tracking the same adults from 2020 to 2025 shows most Americans’ religious affiliation, prayer frequency and service attendance remained steady.

news.title: Religion Remains Stable in the U.S., With Mixed Signals for Young Adults
news.summary_en: There is no clear evidence in the Center’s surveys that any birth cohort that can be tracked over time has become more religious in recent years.

news.title: What We Know About Eligible Voters Who Are Naturalized U.S. Citizens
news.summary_en: Around one-in-ten eligible voters in this year’s midterms are naturalized citizens. See where they live, where they’re from and how they differ demographically.

news.title: What We Learned From a Survey Experiment About Global ‘Superpowers’
news.summary_en: We tested open-ended ways to ask which countries are global superpowers. Here’s what cognitive interviews and a survey experiment revealed.
